title: Swahili Coconut Mandazi
community: Swahili coast — the coconut milk mandazi
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Swahili Coconut Mandazi — mandazi made with fresh coconut milk and a touch of cardamom, producing a richer, more fragrant, and softer result than plain mandazi. The coastal upgrade of Tanzania's everyday fried dough.
longDesc: Coconut mandazi is the coastal version of the mainland's everyday fried dough — the addition of fresh coconut milk produces a mandazi that is richer, softer, and more fragrant. It is the breakfast served at coastal guesthouses and sold at coastal markets.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom, and salt.
Beat egg into warm coconut milk. Add to dry ingredients.
Mix to a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes.
Roll to 1cm. Cut into triangles or circles.
Fry at 170°C 3—4 minutes per side until golden.
chefTips: Coconut milk must be warm — not cold — when adding to the dough.
The dough should be soft but not sticky.
commonMistakes: Cold coconut milk — dough does not come together properly.
cookingScience: See TZA007 for mandazi cooking science.
culturalNote: Coconut mandazi is the coast's morning gift — the same beloved fried dough the whole country eats, but enriched by the coconut that grows on every coastal palm, making it undeniably, unmistakably, coastal Tanzanian.
